PRANAVSAI GANDIKOTA / SOFTWARE ENGINEER

About me.

I'm Pranav, a Computer Science junior at the University of Central Florida, graduating in May 2028 with a 3.99 GPA. I build cloud systems, full-stack applications, and applied AI tools, with a focus on the people using them.

My work has taken me from cloud services at Ford to applied AI research, accessible technology, and platforms for the UCF community.

My experience Read my resume
GitHub LinkedIn Email

At Ford, I migrated six batch processes to Java 21 and Spring Boot on GCP, reducing processing time by 92%, from 45 to 3.5 minutes. I validated 200,000+ records, added 143 tests with over 90% coverage, resolved 31 critical SonarQube findings, and built secret refresh that reloads services in under two minutes without restarts. I also contribute to full-stack development at NextGen Federal.

My work in applied AI includes research at UCF's ISUE Lab, where I fine-tuned three Llama 3.1 8B adapters with QLoRA on 1,820 study examples to predict cognitive load and usability from VR responses. I also built a Python text-to-3D workflow connecting scene extraction, Stable Diffusion 3.5, human review, and TRELLIS, processing 135 images across 30 scene directories and metadata for 48 objects.

I also enjoy building products that people can use directly. As SASE's CS Tech Chair, I lead the web team behind an event platform serving 230+ registered members, with registration, QR attendance, forms, and analytics. I led a six-member team building uKnight, using distributed Redis matchmaking and WebRTC video chat. Other builds include Sentinel for AI-content detection, RePlot for sustainable site discovery, Satchel for shared inventory, ReVision and Vision for accessible interaction, TACO for robotics, Freedom Finances, NextFlix, and Humanotone.

For Paradise, I built a vision-to-haptics navigation pipeline for DeafBlind users. Our team placed 3rd Best Overall among 290+ projects at ShellHacks 2026, with 1,400 hackers participating. Earlier, my 50-page Exodus space-settlement proposal won first prize in the NSS contest among 17,000+ students and 3,000+ entries from 22 countries. I presented the work through oral and poster presentations at ISDC.

Teaching and community work are another part of my time at UCF. I supported 166 students as a Java OOP teaching assistant and led collaborative Computer Science I study sessions as an SI Leader. As AI@UCF Projects Director, I help students turn ideas into working AI projects, and I contribute web design and 3D animation to KnightHacks.

Beyond technical clubs, I planned Diwali and Banquet for UCF's Indian Student Association, bringing together 300+ attendees across the two events, and spoke at Diwali for 250+ attendees. My other experiences include campus outreach with Perplexity, shadowing engineering professionals at BNY, and organizing science fairs and cultural festivals as a school Cultural Secretary. My academic recognitions include Dean's List, President's Honor Roll, Honor Society, and SCLA honors.

Outside of engineering, I love making animations in my free time. I also enjoy piano, filmmaking, and hands-on robotics. I built remote-controlled animatronic heads and published the Unity games Jenny's Playtime on Itch.io and Jumblehot on the Amazon Appstore.
